title: Auditing Financial Crime Controls
summary: How to audit the firm's anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing, sanctions, fraud and anti-bribery controls, aligned with the risk-based approach set out in FATF standards.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to audit the firm's anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing, sanctions, fraud and anti-bribery controls, aligned with the risk-based approach set out in FATF standards.
Learning Objectives: Assess the firm's financial crime risk assessment and control framework
Test customer due diligence, monitoring and reporting effectiveness
Evaluate sanctions screening and fraud controls, including system tuning
Syllabus: Business-wide risk assessment and the risk-based approach
Customer due diligence, ongoing monitoring and suspicious activity reporting
Sanctions screening: lists, thresholds, alerts and testing
Fraud, bribery and the governance of financial crime systems
Intended Audience: Heads of internal audit, audit managers and auditors in banks, insurers, investment firms, fund managers and payment firms
Co-sourced and outsourced audit providers delivering assurance to regulated firms
Audit committee members and compliance and risk staff who rely on internal audit work
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of internal audit, risk or compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. No specialist technical background is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, The Internal Audit Function in Banks (2012)
Institute of Internal Auditors, Global Internal Audit Standards (2024)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
